A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the activation and functional properties of DC are tightly controlled by their metabolic state, and that this metabolic control is exerted by the availability of nutrients and the activity of metabolic enzymes.

DCs are a highly heterogeneous group of cells with a variety of different functional capacities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

DC activation is accompanied by a switch from oxidative phosphorylation to aerobic glycolysis, and that this switch in metabolic pathways underlies the capacity of DCs to perform their function in the context of immunity or tolerance.
DC metabolism is highly dynamic and that metabolic changes are not only induced by activation, but can also be induced by environmental factors such as the presence of pathogens and/or cytokines.
the metabolic state of DCs is a key determinant of DC function, and that targeting DC metabolic pathways may provide a promising new approach to modulate DC function in a clinically relevant manner.
